final_answer:
The ablated versions of LightRAG were analyzed in terms of their performance using NaiveRAG as the reference, across four datasets: Agriculture, CS, Legal, and Mix. These ablated versions include -High (removing low-level retrieval), -Low (removing high-level retrieval), and -Origin (using semantic graphs instead of original text) [1].

1. **-High variant (low-level-only retrieval)**: This variant shows a significant performance decline across nearly all datasets and metrics. The -High variant focuses on specific information and entities but struggles with complex queries that demand comprehensive insights [6].

2. **-Low variant (high-level-only retrieval)**: This variant excels in comprehensiveness by leveraging entity-wise relationships but lacks depth in examining specific entities. While it gathers more extensive and varied information, it may struggle with tasks requiring precise, detailed answers [6].

3. **-Origin variant (semantic graph-based retrieval)**: This variant does not exhibit significant performance declines and even shows improvements in some cases, such as in Agriculture and Mix datasets. The graph-based indexing process effectively extracts key information, providing sufficient context for answering queries while avoiding noise from irrelevant information in the original text [6].

In general, the hybrid mode (full version of LightRAG) combines the strengths of low-level and high-level retrieval, achieving balanced performance across multiple dimensions [6].
